requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. For text that was already agreed or that the user supplied, it MUST direct agents to show the change as a diff against that text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.
rationale:
structural: The requirement text states only what the skill must tell agents to do. It has two parts: don't raise mechanical changes to new text as questions, and show a diff followed by a list of mechanical changes for text already agreed or supplied by the user. It prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type or delegation. The requirement is about the skill's content, so its only implementation root is the skill document. Nothing in the text needs implementation evidence beyond that.

The root `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` meets both clauses in `section[Habeas requirements]/section[Workflow]/paragraph@7b764a629ec4` (step 4). Step 4 says to "Show text that was already agreed or that the user supplied as a diff against that text, then a 'Mechanical:' list of the changes." It also says "Don't raise mechanical changes to new text as questions."

behavioral: The requirement is a content obligation on the bundled `habeas-requirements` skill. It has two parts. (1) The skill must direct agents not to raise mechanical changes to new text as questions. (2) For text already agreed or supplied by the user, the skill must direct agents to show a diff against that text, followed by a list of the mechanical changes.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_shows_mechanical_changes_without_asking]` covers both parts. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`. That helper loads the bundled skill with `bundled_skill`, which joins `SKILL.md` and its reference files and collapses whitespace. It then uses `assert_text` to assert that the text contains each phrase.

- Part 2 is checked by the phrase "Show text that was already agreed or that the user supplied as a diff against that text, then a \"Mechanical:\" list of the changes". It covers the already-agreed and user-supplied scope, the diff, and the Mechanical list that follows it.
- Part 1 is checked by the phrase "Don't raise mechanical changes to new text as questions".

I read the skill text in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`, Workflow step 4. It contains both sentences, so the phrases are real directives rather than incidental text. A skill that left out either directive would fail the test. The distinction between new text and agreed or supplied text is also covered, because each phrase names its own case. The requirement imposes no other behavioral obligations.
